subject: TrustBridge - network + auth follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Brandon Lee <brandon.lee@trustbridge.io>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@trustbridge.io>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps — TrustBridge connectivity, auth, and routing

Hi Brandon / Priya —

Thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed plan so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs we captured:
- Private connectivity: you prefer a VPC endpoint / private onramp over public egress for production.
- Auth model: your security team prefers mutual TLS for service-to-service comms; still open on whether mTLS client certs or token-based mTLS is required for initial onboarding.
- Network controls: IP allowlist for control-plane callbacks, predictable egress IPs for webhooks, and DNS considerations for internal hostnames.
- SDK & structured output: you want the SDK installed in a sidecar, structured JSON outputs for our tool-calling interface, and an embeddings + reranker plan for semantic search.

Action items I captured (owner in parentheses):
1) Provide a concise network checklist + sample VPC endpoint config (Jordan).
2) Share Redwood's recommended mTLS vs API-key tradeoffs and CSR examples (Ben).
3) Draft a short integration plan showing SDK placement, expected ports, and DNS entries (Tessa).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security engineers next week.

Attachments: a quick sketch of what a VPC endpoint into Redwood might look like (trustbridge_network_sketch.png) and a one-page on our private onramp (redwood_secure_onramp.pdf).

Proposed technical deep-dive slots: Tue July 3 10–11am PT or Wed July 4 9–10am PT. If those don't work, send a couple times that do.

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(t) +1 415-555-0119
(attachment: trustbridge_network_sketch.png - 98KB)
(attachment: redwood_secure_onramp.pdf - 210KB)

From: Brandon Lee <brandon.lee@trustbridge.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@trustbridge.io>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — TrustBridge connectivity, auth, and routing

Tessa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the diagram — very helpful. A few clarifying questions before we lock a time: 

1) On VPC endpoints: can Redwood support a private outbound only (no inbound) endpoint that still guarantees a fixed set of egress IPs for callbacks? Our security team is concerned about inbound ports being exposed.
2) mTLS: do you support both mutual TLS with client certs and token-in-TLS (Bearer in TLS) so we can choose? If we go the cert route, do you accept customer-managed CA-signed certs or only Redwood-managed certs?
3) DNS: we have internal split-horizon DNS — if we use a private hostname for the endpoint, will Redwood accept SNI for certificate validation?
4) Ports / NAT: any specific port ranges we should reserve? Will outbound NAT occur from our side or from Redwood-managed gateways when you're issuing callbacks to our webhook endpoints?

We can do Tue July 3 10–11am PT — that works for our infra folks (Priya and I). Please send the invite. Also, attaching our internal network security questionnaire — there are a few fields we'll populate once we confirm approach.

-Brandon
Brandon Lee
Head of Infrastructure, TrustBridge
(attachment: TB_security_questionnaire.xlsx - 42KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: internal checklist for TrustBridge deep-dive (internal)

Team — quick internal plan before we join the call on Tue. Keep this internal-only.

Goal: present a crisp, ops-ready proposal that answers Brandon's security questions and shows low-friction onboarding.

Prep items (short bullets):
- Jordan: produce a one-page VPC endpoint + egress behavior doc (what we require on their VPC, whether we need a customer-managed NAT, and the observed egress IP ranges from Redwood). Include sample AWS CloudFormation snippet we can share.
- Jordan: include whether we can support private outbound-only endpoint (we can; detail how callbacks route over the private channel and when internet fallback occurs).
- Ben: collect mTLS modes we support and examples — client cert flow, token-in-TLS flow, accepted CA options, rotation cadence, and how we log cert fingerprints. Add a short matrix of security pros/cons.
- Tessa: create a focused agenda for the tech call (30–45 min), include goals: agree auth mode, confirm DNS/SNI behavior, decide on SDK placement, and define an embeddings/reranker pilot scope.

Meeting owner: Tessa (lead), Jordan (network lead), Ben (security lead).
Deliverables by Monday EOD: VPC one-pager, mTLS matrix, draft agenda.

I'll also prepare a short example policy for IP allowlists and expected webhook TTL behavior.

-ben
Ben Carter
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: internal_vpc_template.yaml - 6KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Brandon Lee <brandon.lee@trustbridge.io>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@trustbridge.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-05T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Confirming Tue 3 Jul deep-dive + artifacts attached

Brandon / Priya —

Thanks — confirmed for Tue July 3 10–11am PT. Invite sent (Zoom link in calendar).

Quick attachments so your infra team has something to review beforehand: 
- VPC endpoint sketch + minimal CloudFormation snippet (trustbridge_network_sketch.png)
- One-pager describing our supported mTLS and token-in-TLS options with rotation notes (redwood_secure_onramp.pdf)
- A short checklist for embedding & reranker pilot (inline below).

Embedding/Reranker pilot checklist (suggested minimal scope):
- Dataset slice: 10k documents (Priya to confirm), baseline embed model and reranker candidate.
- SDK placement: sidecar vs managed outbound (if you pick private onramp, sidecar recommended for latency).
- Structured output: we'll demonstrate tool-calling with typed JSON responses and a thin schema contract.
- Observability: token-level latency metrics and per-route cost estimate during pilot.

If anything above looks off, flag it now and we'll adjust before the call. Looking forward — talk Tuesday.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
